answer: Agents can require a newcomer to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its actions count toward rewards or votes. The protocol assigns each identity a small random task; inconsistent or duplicate answers expose coordinated accounts, and proven fraud burns their stake. A gale of disposable profiles may reach the jetty, but each must tie up real capital, while a zephyr of cheap retries cannot recover slashed funds. This raises the cost of sybil attacks without assuming identities are perfectly verified.
